dimensions.name: Problem & literature orientation

evidence.note: Read perfect.align and the graph header, and specifically read the node→edge transition line to understand the exact file format before coding.
Wrote analyze_graphs.py to probe node/edge counts and degree distributions, and wrote evaluator.py reproducing S3/NC exactly, validating it against the provided reference alignment.
Web-searched S3/PPI alignment literature and specifically SANA/L-GRAAL DM-HS S3 scores and seeding — recognizing and naming established methods for this problem class.

Aligner designed to warm-start from the reference alignment with an NC floor, and correctly treated the reference S3 (0.248) as a starting point rather than a ceiling — instance-specific leverage of the provided reference.
Implemented multiple established methods (SA-on-S3, topological signatures, seed-and-extend, percolation matching) synthesized against the actual networks.
Reasoned explicitly about minimizing E2_aligned in the S3 denominator to justify random-start over hub-matching — analysis directly shaping the objective/algorithm.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent fully satisfies anchor 8: it parsed the format precisely, reproduced and validated S3/NC, deliberately researched specific named methods (SANA annealing-on-S3, seed-and-extend, topological signatures, L-GRAAL), and probed the real networks' sizes and degree distributions. It reaches into anchor 10 by exploiting the reference alignment as a warm start (and correctly recognizing it is not an S3 upper bound) and by reasoning about the S3 denominator to shape the objective. It stops short of a perfect 10 because it never explicitly identified/leveraged the Yeast2KReduced⊂SC subset structure and some instance reasoning came mid-optimization rather than fully upfront, placing it at 9.

dimensions.name: Pipeline decomposition across two deliverables

evidence.note: Explicitly built shared infrastructure as separable sub-goals: a parser (analyze_graphs.py) then an independent S3/NC scorer (evaluator.py) validated on the perfect reference before any aligning — factoring reusable tooling from deliverable-specific work.

Wrote a single generic reusable aligner.cpp supporting both random and reference-seeded starts, SA, and an optional NC constraint — one shared toolchain intended for both deliverables rather than duplicated per-instance code.
Sequenced deliverables: tackled y2kr-SC (dual S3>=0.55 + NC>=0.30 milestone) first, treating both numeric thresholds as concrete done-checks, deploying only after verifying 0.559/0.3001.

For DM-HS treated seeding+optimization as its own sub-goal with checkpoints, adapting the decomposition across multiple seed strategies (topo signature, seed-extend, percolation) based on intermediate S3 readings.

Reallocated the bulk of effort to the harder-to-crack DM-HS 0.32 bar via staged random-start SA, then iterative reheating rounds 1-4 and hill-climbing refinement — each round measured against the numeric target; later rounds became repetitive rather than newly re-decomposed.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly factored shared infrastructure (parser, S3/NC scorer, generic configurable aligner) from per-instance tuning, marked every milestone with its numeric bar (0.55/0.30/0.32), and deliberately sequenced the two deliverables — matching anchor 8. It also shows anchor-10 traits: treating the optimization loop as its own checkpointed sub-goal and adapting investment toward the harder DM-HS target as intermediate scores revealed the gap. It falls short of a full 10 because the ordering rationale wasn't framed as easy-vs-hard and the late reheating rounds were repetitive rather than fresh re-decomposition, so I place it at 8.

dimensions.name: Faithful local metric self-checking

evidence.note: Wrote evaluator.py to compute S3 and NC 'exactly as specified' — an independent scorer matching the grader's metric.

Ran the evaluator on the provided perfect reference alignment to verify its scores — a partial validation that cross-checks the NC computation against the reference (perfect align should give NC=1.0).

Consistently ran the independent evaluator on each candidate alignment to confirm exact S3/NC before deploying, and did a final verification of both deliverables — the scorer drives the accept/deploy decision.

Aligner optimizes S3 directly as its objective with an NC>=0.30 constraint; mapping is a permutation by construction so injectivity is structurally guaranteed, but no explicit format-validity check (name match/coverage) is described.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent implemented an independent S3/NC scorer matching the spec and used it consistently to confirm each deliverable cleared its thresholds before finishing, clearly meeting anchor 5. It also validated the NC computation by running on the provided perfect reference alignment, pushing it above a bare 5. However, it stops short of anchor 8: no tiny hand-computable test of the S3 denominator's E2_aligned term, no explicit enforcement of file validity (exact node names, full coverage) beyond structural injectivity, and no second-method score triangulation. This places the observed behavior at a 6.

dimensions.name: Tracking score progress over optimization runs

evidence.note: Established reference S3/NC baseline via evaluator, and tracked exact best-so-far scores per run (yeast Run 3 S3=0.559346 NC=0.3001), showing a maintained score ledger against targets.
Repeated sleep+tail log monitoring of parallel optimization jobs during long stochastic runs — logs the objective over iterations rather than running blind.
Killed still-running jobs early once finished runs already had better scores — used live monitoring to reallocate compute.

Tracked DM-HS best-so-far progression (0.3073→0.3112→0.3122→0.3131→0.3131) across reheating rounds, always deploying/re-evaluating the best; clearly knew DM-HS still missed the 0.32 bar while yeast was done.
Weakness: interpreted a clear plateau (~0.311-0.313) as being 'on a direct trajectory to cross 0.32' repeatedly, failing to diagnose genuine convergence — keeps it below the top anchor.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent logged the objective over iterations, monitored parallel runs periodically, maintained an explicit best-so-far ledger per deliverable, and used that information to kill/deploy/reheat and to know which file still fell short — squarely matching the level-8 anchor. It falls short of 10 because it repeatedly misread a hard plateau at ~0.313 as continued progress toward 0.32 rather than detecting convergence, so it did not cleanly distinguish genuine plateau from slow progress.

dimensions.name: Course-correction when a target is missed

evidence.note: When early yeast runs plateaued the agent changed meaningful levers: made temperatures configurable to switch between hill-climbing and SA, then added sideways moves to traverse plateaus — targeted mechanism changes, then re-measured.

For DM-HS the agent cycled through distinct initialization strategies (topological signatures, seed-and-extend, wiring-aware percolation) and then made a major algorithm change (topologically-guided local move generator) rather than re-running the same greedy match.

Genuine bottleneck diagnosis: reasoned from the S3 formula that hub-matching bias inflates E2_aligned in the denominator, so switched to random-start SA to find sparser mappings — hypothesis-driven, metric-aware course correction (anchor-8 behavior).

Reheating rounds 1-4 largely repeat the same intervention with only slightly-tuned temperatures, all converging ~0.311-0.313 without a new hypothesis for the 0.32 barrier — a trivial-tweak pattern that keeps this below a clean 10.
Preserved best-known solutions (risk-free hill climbing, evaluating multiple candidate files to select the best) and decisively killed lingering/inferior runs, deploying the best alignment.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds anchor 5 (changing meaningful levers and re-measuring) and hits anchor 8: it diagnoses WHY targets are missed — notably the E2_aligned/hub-bias reasoning at step 172 — then makes targeted changes (random init, annealing schedules, guided move generator, sideways moves) and re-measures, while preserving best solutions and abandoning dead ends. It falls short of a clean 10 because the late-stage DM-HS reheating rounds repeat essentially the same lever with only trivial temperature tweaks and no fresh hypothesis about the persistent 0.32 plateau.

dimensions.name: Optimizer compute-budget allocation

evidence.note: Ran a 10M-iteration probe explicitly to measure speed and S3 improvement, checked CPU core count, then launched 4 parallel seeded runs — deliberate calibration before committing to a large search.
Scaled full runs up to 1.5B then 1.8B iterations across 4 cores after cheap probes established the rate — right-sized big runs following small ones.
Repeatedly re-engineered the aligner (flat matrix, 32-bit offsets) and benchmarked to raise iterations/sec, treating compute as a scarce resource to be maximized.

Banked and verified a best solution for each deliverable so a valid output was always in place; yeast solved and banked early while the harder DM-HS received most of the budget (difficulty-based allocation).
Many reheating/refinement rounds threw ~1B-1.8B iterations each for tiny gains (0.311→0.313), never reaching 0.32 — failed to recognize marginal-return exhaustion, keeping it short of a clean 10.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent deliberately sized its search with cheap 10M probes, benchmarked iterations/sec, parallelized across all cores, continually banked a safe best solution, and split budget between the two pairs by difficulty — squarely matching the level-8 anchor and touching several level-10 behaviors (probes, parallelization, checkpointing, banking). It stops short of a full 10 because it kept pouring billions of iterations into DM-HS for negligible score gains without recognizing that marginal returns no longer justified the compute.

rubric.task_read: A long-horizon, open-ended research/optimization task: align two pairs of PPI networks to hit specific S3 (and NC) thresholds. Difficulty comes from network alignment being NP-hard (warranting literature reuse, e.g. SANA/MAGNA/GHOST), from two separate deliverables with different bars, and crucially from the fact that S3/NC are fully computable locally — so the payoff hinges on building a faithful self-check and iterating a stochastic optimizer against it under a compute budget. A skilled practitioner invests heavily in orientation, verification, and adaptive iteration; decomposition is moderate.

dimensions.name: Problem & literature orientation
dimensions.description: Understanding the graph format, the exact S3/NC definitions, and surveying known network-alignment methods before committing to an approach.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Network alignment is NP-hard; naive greedy approaches rarely clear S3>=0.55. Reusing proven algorithms (SANA and its simulated-annealing S3 objective, MAGNA, GHOST, sequence+topology seeds) is the difference between hitting and missing thresholds. Misreading the S3 denominator or the injectivity requirement silently poisons everything downstream.

anchors.0: Starts coding an alignment with no inspection of the graph files or the metric definitions.
anchors.3: Reads the graph format and metric formulas superficially; picks the first idea (e.g. degree-sorted greedy) with no awareness of the field.
anchors.5: Correctly parses the format, reproduces S3 and NC definitions accurately, and recognizes this as a known problem class, naming at least one established method to base work on.
anchors.8: Deliberately researches specific network-alignment methods (e.g. SANA's annealing-on-S3, seed-and-extend, topological signatures), and probes the actual networks (sizes, degree distributions, whether the provided y2kr-SC-perfect.align can seed or bound the search) to choose an approach fit to THIS data.
anchors.10: Synthesizes multiple methods against the concrete instance: quantifies network sizes/density, reasons about what S3 level is achievable, notices instance-specific leverage (e.g. Yeast2KReduced⊂SC structure, exploiting the reference alignment as a warm start or upper bound), and lets that analysis directly shape the algorithm and objective before heavy coding.

dimensions.name: Pipeline decomposition across two deliverables
dimensions.description: Breaking work into ordered sub-goals (parser → scorer → aligner → optimizer → two outputs) each with a done-check, and sequencing the two independent deliverables sensibly.
dimensions.why_it_matters: There are two distinct targets with different thresholds and a shared toolchain. Building the scorer and a reusable aligner first, then applying to both pairs, avoids duplicated effort and lets each threshold be a concrete milestone.

anchors.0: Treats the whole thing as one undifferentiated blob; no separable steps.
anchors.3: Vague ordering in prose; no explicit done-criteria per step.
anchors.5: Clear stages (parse, score, align, optimize, write files) with the two thresholds treated as explicit milestones per deliverable.
anchors.8: Structured plan that factors shared infrastructure (parser, S3/NC scorer, generic aligner) from per-instance tuning, sequences the easier DM-HS (single S3 bar) vs the harder y2kr-SC (S3+NC) deliberately, and marks each milestone with the numeric bar it must clear.
anchors.10: Milestone structure that also anticipates the optimization loop as its own sub-goal with intermediate checkpoints (e.g. 'reach S3=0.4 by iteration N, else re-seed'), and adapts the decomposition as intermediate scores reveal which deliverable needs more investment.

dimensions.name: Faithful local metric self-checking
dimensions.description: Building an independent scorer that computes S3 and NC exactly as specified, plus validating output-file well-formedness (injective mapping, exact node names, every V1 node covered).
dimensions.why_it_matters: The grader's metric is fully reproducible offline. An agent that implements S3/NC faithfully can measure itself against the thresholds before submitting; one that assumes success or mis-implements the denominator will ship failing files while believing they pass. This is the single highest-leverage meta-move on this task.

anchors.0: No local scoring; submits alignments without measuring S3/NC.
anchors.3: Some ad hoc sanity check (e.g. counts lines) but no correct S3 computation, or a scorer with an unverified/wrong formula.
anchors.5: Implements an S3/NC scorer matching the spec and uses it to confirm each deliverable clears its threshold before finishing.
anchors.8: Scorer is validated for correctness (e.g. cross-checked on a tiny hand-computable case, and NC checked against the provided reference), AND file validity is enforced (injectivity, exact name match, full coverage) so the optimizer's reported score provably equals what the grader will see.
anchors.10: Verification is airtight and drives the whole loop: the S3 scorer is the optimizer's objective, independently re-derived/tested against edge cases (denominator's E2_aligned term, disconnected nodes), NC and format validity are continuously asserted, and the agent guards against overfitting-to-a-bug by triangulating the score more than one way.

dimensions.name: Tracking score progress over optimization runs
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of current S3/NC vs targets across (potentially long) stochastic optimization, detecting plateaus/thrashing and knowing which deliverable still falls short.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Simulated-annealing / iterative aligners run for many iterations with noisy improvement. Without tracking the objective over time the agent can burn the budget on a converged run, or believe it's improving when it's stuck, or forget which of the two files still misses its bar.

anchors.0: No visibility into intermediate scores; runs something once and hopes.
anchors.3: Checks a final score but has no sense of trajectory or whether the optimizer plateaued.
anchors.5: Monitors S3 (and NC) periodically during optimization and knows, per deliverable, the gap to target at any point.
anchors.8: Logs the objective over iterations, recognizes convergence vs continued gains, and uses that to decide when to stop, restart, or reallocate time between the two deliverables rather than running blind.
anchors.10: Maintains a disciplined running ledger of best-so-far scores, distinguishes genuine plateau from slow progress, detects thrashing/regression early, and allocates remaining compute where the marginal score gain is highest across both deliverables.

dimensions.name: Course-correction when a target is missed
dimensions.description: Revising algorithm, seeding, objective, or parameters when a deliverable stalls below its threshold, rather than repeating a converged run.
dimensions.why_it_matters: A first approach (e.g. greedy topological match) may plateau below S3=0.55 or NC=0.30. Progress requires switching strategy — better seeds, annealing, sequence signals, exploiting the reference alignment for the yeast pair — instead of re-running the same thing.

anchors.0: Barrels ahead on the initial approach even when it clearly falls short; never changes tack.
anchors.3: Reruns the same method with trivial tweaks hoping for luck; no diagnosis of why it's stuck.
anchors.5: When a threshold is missed, changes a meaningful lever (parameters, seeding, or algorithm) and re-measures.
anchors.8: Diagnoses WHY a target is missed (e.g. S3 plateau implies weak topological matching; NC gap implies wrong node correspondence), then makes a targeted change — better initialization, annealing schedule, or exploiting the reference alignment for the yeast NC bar — and confirms the change helped.
anchors.10: Runs a genuine improvement cycle: hypothesis about the bottleneck → targeted intervention → re-measure → keep/revert, escalating from cheap tweaks to algorithm swaps as evidence warrants, and abandons dead ends decisively while preserving best-known solutions.

dimensions.name: Optimizer compute-budget allocation
dimensions.description: Calibrating optimizer runtime/iterations/restarts against wall-clock so both thresholds are actually reached within available time.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Stochastic network aligners can run arbitrarily long; a HSapiens-scale search is expensive. Deciding iteration counts, restarts, and how to split a finite budget between the two deliverables is a distinct allocation problem beyond just watching scores.

anchors.0: No regard for runtime; either a single under-powered run or an unbounded run that never returns a usable result.
anchors.3: Picks arbitrary iteration counts with no relation to observed convergence or time cost.
anchors.5: Chooses run lengths informed by how long a run takes and how fast the score improves, ensuring both files get produced.
anchors.8: Deliberately sizes the search (early cheap runs to estimate convergence, then a right-sized full run), and splits budget between the two pairs according to their difficulty and remaining gap.
anchors.10: Treats compute as a scarce resource optimized explicitly: uses small probes to calibrate, scales up only where marginal score justifies it, parallelizes or checkpoints long runs, and keeps a safe best solution banked at all times so time pressure never yields an empty or invalid deliverable.
